Subject: Follow-up: POC success criteria and access (Helio)

Hi Alex — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to kick off the POC days:  

Key success criteria (as I heard on the call):
- 95th percentile inference latency < 120ms for 512-token requests against your anonymized clinical prompt set
- Per-session cost under $0.015/token for steady-state traffic (projected)
- No PII leakage in inferred outputs (you flagged de-identification tests)
- SSO integration and audit logs visible in the console for at least two engineering users

Immediate items we need from Helio to start provisioning your trial environment:
1) SSO invitation (SAML/Okta) for the two pilot users (alex.turner@heliohealth.com, sec@heliohealth.com).
2) IP allowlist for your staging testers (range: 34.120.0.0/18 or confirm alternate ranges).
3) Example prompt set (10 representative prompts) and a small sample dataset (anonymized).

I've attached a short POC requirements template to capture owners, timelines, and test vectors — please fill the left column and return. Once we have SSO and IP ranges we can issue a temporary API key and spin up a dedicated sandbox project.

Attachment: Helio_POC_requirements_template.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

Next proposed timeline:
- 10/6: SSO invites + IP allowlist completed by Helio security
- 10/7: Redwood provisions sandbox + temp API key, sends instructions
- 10/12–10/23: Evaluation window (2 weeks of tests)

Owners:
- Redwood: Sean (trial ops), Monica (provisioning / support), Rishi (security liaison)
- Helio: Alex (product lead), Security team (sec@heliohealth.com)

If that looks right I can ask Monica to kick off the provisioning once you confirm the IP ranges and SSO method.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you running.

—
